messages:
jen_support: FYI customer reported a billing spike + 403s after a recent identity sync. They say multiple service accounts were re-created and tokens invalidated. full ticket: https://support.example/t/7893 :eyes:

sam_sre: Can you paste the first failing request ID and any API error body? 403 could be KMS decryption or authz.

jen_support: request id `r-0a1b2c3d`, error body: `{"code":403,"message":"KMS: decrypt failed: access denied"}` Customer's note: SCIM trace shows duplicate user records created within 2s window.

priya_security: @jen_support tagging security — if SCIM created duplicate service accounts that could've rotated keys or triggered re-provisioning flows. We need audit logs for SCIM create/delete + KMS key usage for that tenant.

matt_eng: Also want to know whether the SAML assertion replay triggered a reprovision, or if the SCIM connector retried and created two entries. Do we have connector timeout/retry logs?

jen_support: Attaching minimal repro from customer logs: ```
POST /scim/v2/Users 2026-01-24T18:12:03Z -> 201 created id:svc-123
POST /scim/v2/Users 2026-01-24T18:12:04Z -> 201 created id:svc-124
PUT /kms/decrypt 2026-01-24T18:12:07Z -> 403 
Error: KMS access denied for key proj-tenant-key
```

olivia_prod: This looks like a race where SCIM retries didn't dedupe, then the second identity got a separate service account and new key material. Our KMS policy might only allow the original service account principal. If the customer rotated keys, older tokens could fail.

priya_security: Requesting these from infra team: 
- Audit log slice for scim.user.create, scim.user.delete for tenant `acme-corp` ±5min of 18:12:00
- KMS access logs for key `proj-tenant-key` same window
- Any deploys/rollouts touching provisioner in that window

sam_sre: I'll pull the audit logs and share a redacted extract. Quick check in splunk shows two scim.create events spaced 1s apart from IP 52.10.11.8 and 52.10.11.8 (same IP) with identical external_id. That suggests retries from the customer's SCIM client.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: provisioner-service v1.14.2 -> v1.14.3 at 2026-01-24T17:59:12Z on cluster-prod-2.

matt_eng: Hmm deploy 17:59 could have changed retry logic? But it's 13 minutes before incident. Need the changelog for 1.14.3. @olivia_prod can you confirm if 1.14.3 changed idempotency/dedup?

olivia_prod: 1.14.3 included a fix for exponential backoff timing but not dedupe. It actually reduced the default timeout so some clients might retry faster. I'm filing an action: add idempotency-token header support to the provisioner.

jen_support: Customer says billing anomaly is tokens minted twice and usage counted separately — they want refund + root cause.

priya_security: Root cause action items: 
1) Confirm SCIM duplicates were client retries (evidence: identical external_id + same IP).
2) Confirm provisioner didn't dedupe on external_id.
3) Confirm KMS policy only grants decrypt to original service account principal (svc-123) and not to duplicated svc-124.
4) Provide customer with purge/remediation steps and offer temporary rollback token or key binding.

sam_sre: I attached redacted audit snippet: ```
[2026-01-24T18:12:03Z] scim.create user external_id: ext-42 -> svc-123 principal: scim-proxy@52.10.11.8
[2026-01-24T18:12:04Z] scim.create user external_id: ext-42 -> svc-124 principal: scim-proxy@52.10.11.8
[2026-01-24T18:12:07Z] kms.decrypt key: proj-tenant-key principal: svc-124 -> DENY
[2026-01-24T18:12:07Z] kms.decrypt key: proj-tenant-key principal: svc-123 -> ALLOW
```

matt_eng: That proves it. svc-124 doesn't have key binding. For immediate mitigation: grant temporary decrypt to svc-124 OR delete svc-124 and reissue tokens for svc-123. Which does the customer prefer?

jen_support: Customer prefers we avoid deleting accounts; asked for temporary decrypt grant while they patch client. They also want steps to prevent reoccurrence.

priya_security: Security prefers not to expand key bindings broadly. Propose: create a short-lived admin token bound to svc-124 scoped to decrypt only for the next 1h, log all usage, then revoke. Also require customer to implement idempotency-token or dedupe by external_id.

olivia_prod: Agree. I'll schedule a quick patch to accept an Idempotency-Key header and ignore creates when external_id exists. Low-risk patch, target next release.

sam_sre: Operational steps I'm taking now: 
- Applied temporary KMS allow rule: principal svc-124 -> decrypt for key proj-tenant-key until 2026-01-24T19:40:00Z (one hour)
- Notified customer via ticket, asked them to stop retries and apply client fix

jen_support: Customer confirmed they can pause sync. They've accepted temporary grant. They're asking for an audit bundle showing create/delete events + KMS grants for their compliance team.

priya_security: We'll produce the redacted bundle (events + KMS ACL entries) and redact unrelated tenants. I'll own that report.

matt_eng: After patch, we should add an integration test simulating duplicate scim creates and ensure provisioner dedupes on external_id. Also add a canary that detects sudden double-creates per external_id within short window and alerts.

jen_support: Thanks all — closing loop with customer. Key live items: temporary KMS grant applied, security to deliver audit bundle, product to add idempotency header support, eng to add regression test + canary.

olivia_prod: I'll open a small RFC and link it here: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/SCIM-idempotency-2026

jen_support: marking resolved for now, will re-open if anything else pops up :white_check_mark:
